explain.say: Imagine building a whole town on top of a steep mountain, high in the clouds, with no iron tools and no wheels. Around 1450, the Inca did it! Look at the chain: these are the steps for building Machu Picchu in Peru.

explain.say: The topsoil, for growing food! Well done. Wow fact: an engineer worked out that about six tenths of Machu Picchu's building work is hidden underground, in foundations and drains. That is why it still stands after 500 years.

faq.a: Inca workers split granite on the mountain, shaped it with hammerstones and fitted blocks without mortar. They built terraces and drains so the town would not wash away.

faq.q: Why do Inca walls survive earthquakes?
faq.a: The stones fit tightly with no mortar, walls lean slightly inward, and doors are wider at the bottom. In a quake the stones shift and settle back into place.
asks: Why are Inca walls so strong?

faq.q: Why does Machu Picchu not wash away?
faq.a: It gets heavy rain, so the Inca built terraces with layers of stone, gravel and sand, and over a hundred drainage channels, to carry water safely away.
asks: How did the Inca stop landslides?

faq.a: Local Quechua farmers always knew about it. In 1911, they guided the American explorer Hiram Bingham there, and he made it famous around the world.
asks: Did Hiram Bingham discover Machu Picchu?

faq.a: Around 1450, probably as an estate for the Inca ruler Pachacuti. It was left about a hundred years later, and the Spanish invaders never found it.

facts: Machu Picchu was built around 1450 for the Inca ruler Pachacuti, at about 2,430 metres above sea level.
Inca builders fitted granite blocks without mortar, a style called ashlar masonry.

quiz.say: What did the Inca use to hold Machu Picchu's best walls together?
quiz.show: What did the Inca use to hold Machu Picchu's best walls together?
quiz.why: The blocks were shaped to fit so tightly that no mortar was needed.

wrong.0: The finest Inca walls used no cement or mortar at all.
wrong.2: The Inca did not use iron tools or nails.

quiz.say: Why did the terraces have layers of gravel and stones under the soil?
quiz.show: Why did the terraces have layers of gravel and stones under the soil?
quiz.why: The layers let rainwater drain, so the soil and slopes did not slide away.

wrong.1: The layers were for drainage, not warmth.
wrong.2: The goal was to move water out, not to add weight.
